findings.evidence: /tmp/ih7/mem.mjs (raw-byte child, one legal output frame of 64 MiB at cap 64 MiB + exit) → stdout 67108864, consumer peak RSS +419 MiB (~6.5× cap); prior verify probe a4 (protocol code unchanged): 1e6 legal 1-byte frames at default 1 MiB cap → RSS peak +96 MiB.
findings.summary: README now says consumer memory is "bounded by the output cap: about 2× the cap while a frame is in flight" — true for held memory, untrue for RSS (transient ~6.5× cap for a cap frame, ~96× default cap for a tiny-frame flood); ADR-0557 §6 states held ~2× + "a few × cap transient RSS" correctly. "Its" also reads as the child. Wording: say held ~2× cap, transient RSS several × cap.

findings.evidence: probe.mjs a4: 1e6 legal 1-byte output frames in one 8 MB write at default 1 MiB cap → resolved, stdout 1e6, consumer RSS peak +96.2 MiB, max loop lag 63 ms; a16 4e6 @ 4 MB cap → +180 MiB; a17 16e6 @ 16 MB cap → +214 MiB (sublinear, transient).
findings.summary: Per-frame slice allocation makes a hostile tiny-frame flood at the default cap peak consumer RSS ~96 MiB (Acceptance 14 holds honest write shapes < 64 MiB; Acceptance 13 bounds only held heap, which holds).
